name: Fastbreak
label: Revelation
lede: Fastbreak started in a Connecticut suburb at fifteen, named their first album after a Jerky Boys prank call, moved to Boston, signed to Revelation, and called it quits in 2000.

eras.title: Not old school, the only school
eras.text: Fastbreak began as middle-schoolers in Bethel, a suburb of Danbury, Connecticut, in the shadow of an older local band, Cornerstone, whose bassist was singer Patrick Rorick's brother Kevin. When Cornerstone ended, Fastbreak inherited its crowd, its motto and two of its members.

years.h: Four teenagers in Bethel, Connecticut, average age fifteen
years.p: Revelation says Fastbreak start as a four-piece averaging fifteen years old. They take Cornerstone's motto, Not Old School, The Only School, as their own.
years.xp: No Echo has Rorick and St. Clair placing the band's start in middle school, a little earlier than the 1994 Revelation gives. Their first hardcore show was opening for Cornerstone, the local band they were already following.

years.h: Cornerstone ends, and Fastbreak get the room
years.p: Cornerstone, the older Connecticut band with Patrick Rorick's brother Kevin on bass and two future Fastbreak members, breaks up. Its crowd moves over.
years.xp: Cornerstone's lineup, per No Echo: Toby on vocals, Kevin Rorick on bass, Steve Pica on guitar, Tyler Wragg on drums. Pica is on Revelation's Fastbreak lineup too.

years.h: Two 7"s in one year, and New Jersey notices
years.p: After the Youth Pride demo, Fastbreak release Don't Stop Trying on Third Party Records and Where It Lies on Stand Hard Records.
years.xp: Stand Hard was run by Jesse Gustafson, who also played in Tenfold, Follow Through and Right Brigade. Where It Lies was pressed at 250 copies.

years.h: Neal St. Clair joins, and Shutdown take them out of New England
years.p: Guitarist Neal St. Clair comes in. A summer tour with New York's Shutdown is Fastbreak's first outside New England.

eras.title: Fast cars, a prank call, a move to Boston
eras.text: Boston's Big Wheel Recreation put out Fastbreak's first album, in art that pointedly didn't look youth crew. By the end of 1998 the band was moving to Boston, where guitarist Neal St. Clair and drummer Luke Garro were also playing in In My Eyes.

yt: Full set at the CT Bike Exchange, Bristol, Jan. 17, 1998
years.h: Fast Cars, Fast Women comes out on Big Wheel Recreation
years.p: Recorded January and February 1998 with producer Dean Baltulonis, with art direction by Rama Mayo. The title is a line from a Jerky Boys prank call.
years.xp:
Big Wheel was Mayo's label and studio. The design came from Josh Hooten of Punk Planet, with photography by Paul Drake.

Around then Fat Wreck Chords sent a rejection letter addressed to Fatbreak. Rorick and St. Clair still laugh about it. Iodine Recordings later reissued the album, remastered, with demos and expanded packaging.

years.h: Four weeks across the country with [[Ten Yard Fight|c051f242-5907-42ce-b25f-678f14323dac]]
years.p: A summer 1998 tour with Boston's Ten Yard Fight carries the Connecticut band to California.

years.h: Rorick and Raymond follow to Boston in the fall
years.p: St. Clair is already there. By late 1998 the rest arrive, and he and drummer Luke Garro are also in In My Eyes.

eras.title: Whenever you're ready, then done
eras.text: Revelation signed Fastbreak off a cassette, and the second album went more melodic and more personal, closer to Lifetime and later Gorilla Biscuits. It split the audience, and a long European tour wore the band down.

years.h: A cassette in Boston ends up on Revelation's desk
years.p: Revelation A&R Jason Upright hears two Fastbreak demo tracks on the B side of a tape that Big Wheel Recreation sent over, and signs them.
years.xp: Equal Vision, Vagrant and Initial Records were also interested. Revelation didn't tell the band what to play, but pushed their image in ads, which Rorick later regretted.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.p: Made on about a $5,000 budget, with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] and Lifetime in its melodies and Patrick Rorick's most inward lyrics. Revelation's first vinyl run was 226 copies on yellow.

years.cap: Fastbreak on stage, Dec. 3, 1999, on the European tour with Cause for Alarm
years.h: Four weeks in Europe with [[Cause for Alarm|1940001f-3270-4d87-9501-eb243d5f9f50]]
years.p: Booked by M.A.D., the tour runs more than four weeks. Some shows land, others leave Fastbreak feeling isolated.
years.xp:
The tour came out of the Revelation signing. Earlier that summer the band had done six weeks in the US with [[Farside|c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069]] and [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]].

Back home, hardcore was moving toward darker bands such as Blood for Blood and American Nightmare, and Whenever You're Ready sat badly with the core audience.

years.cap: Fastbreak live, Dec. 3, 1999, Europe, with Cause for Alarm
years.p: The new songs weren't connecting, and singing such personal material fed Patrick Rorick's anxiety and depression, he told No Echo.
years.xp:
Rorick didn't want Fastbreak to be part of the music business, and the label-to-Vagrant route open to bands then left him uneasy. Drummer Luke Garro went on to [[Piebald|403bc4cd-602c-4b59-8379-05cb24f66aa6]], and bassist Don Raymond eventually played with [[The Format|81b07a2a-cdf0-4c5e-a68c-8d910e1f0ea6]]. Rorick turned to spiritual pursuits and stayed away for years.

Early guitarist Chris Legg, later of Break Faith, has since died.

eras.title: A guitar shop in Riverside
eras.text: Neal St. Clair's son Tate started his own hardcore band in Los Angeles, Start Today, and that pulled Fastbreak out of retirement for one unannounced set.

q: literally felt like a Fastbreak show from 1996
years.h: Three of Fastbreak open for [[Piebald|403bc4cd-602c-4b59-8379-05cb24f66aa6]] in a Riverside guitar shop
years.p: No announcement. Don Raymond flies in, Patrick Rorick sits out, and the set is five songs. St. Clair's son Tate, who plays in Los Angeles hardcore band Start Today, helped set it up.
years.xp: It was the first Fastbreak show in 24 years.
